rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Mixture vs compound:** air is a mixture (variable composition); water is a compound (fixed H:O = 1:8 by mass).  ·  **Chemistry is "central"** — it links physics (laws) with biology (life processes).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Chemistry is the science of the composition, structure, properties and reactions of matter."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Water (H₂O)*** — a compound: fixed 2:1 atom ratio, decomposable by electrolysis into H₂ and O₂.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Central Science Chemistry studies matter — its composition, structure, properties and the changes it undergoes. Sitting between physics and biology, it is called the **central science**: it explains materials, medicines, fuels, fertilisers and life's own molecules in one framework.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Definition and scope **Chemistry** is the branch of science that deals with the composition, structure, properties of matter and the changes (reactions) it undergoes, together with the energy changes accompanying them.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Element → one atom type; compound → fixed ratio, chemical bonds; mixture → variable, physical separation."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Differentiate element, compound and mixture with one example each.** — Element: one kind of atom, cannot be decomposed (Fe). Compound: two+ elements in fixed ratio, chemically combined, separable only chemically (H₂O). Mixture: variable composition, separable physically (air).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Give one example per branch — examples earn marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Pure substance vs mixture** — fixed composition and chemical separation only apply to pure substances.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Chemistry = composition + structure + properties + changes of matter. Branches: physical, inorganic, organic, analytical, biochemical, applied.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Everything you can touch, see or breathe is matter — chemistry's subject matter is literally the material world.

rows.label: MCQ drill
